newsitem.title: CHINA: China First Auto to call for resumed car finance.
newsitem.headline: China First Auto to call for resumed car finance.

text.p: China's First Automotive Corp will appeal to the central government to permit a resumption of car financing to help revive flagging domestic sales, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

First Automotive Corp (FAC) would join with finance partner the Construction Bank of China to ask Beijing to reinstate an installment buying plan started last May but suspended in September, the newspaper quoted FAC vice-president Wu Wei as saying.

"With the halt in bank loans for installment purchases of cars, the automotive market... has been plunged once again into a depression," said the newspaper, which is published by the official China Daily.
Bankers have said that the central bank ordered a halt to the car loans because it was concerned the plan would excessively stimulate spending.
FAC is the distributor of cars produced by FAW (First Automotive Works)-Volkswagen Automotive Co, a joint venture with German automaker Volkswagen AG.
Suspension of the credit plan had caused a drop in sales of FAW-Volkswagen's popular Jetta sedan, the newspaper said without elaborating.
"An improved national market is urgently needed by... FAW-Volkswagen... to take advantage of its newly enlarged production capacity and pay back large loan amounts beginning next year," it said.
FAW-Volkswagen would have to pay back loans and interest totalling 1.0 billion yuan ($120 million), it said.
The firm would try to export more of its engines and expand its product line to try to recoup losses in the domestic market, the newspaper quoted company vice-president Herbert Lederle as saying.
The company had sold 60,000 Jettas since it opened in 1991, it said.
FAW-Volkswagen would from this year gradually take over distribution of its products from FAC, it said but gave no further details.
